name: replace-text
description:
The phrase changed by pairs, one after the other (a later pair works on the result of the earlier ones).

by: what a pair finds:
- "substring": every occurrence of the text, in any case and ё as е, becomes the replacement as given;
- "phrase": a phrase equal to the text (case, ё and extra spaces do not count) becomes the replacement in the case of the phrase: lower, capitalised or upper («МОСКВА» → «САНКТ-ПЕТЕРБУРГ»);
- "regex": each match of the pattern (cyrillic letters are word chars) becomes the replacement, with `\1` and `\g<name>` for the groups.
first_only: with "regex", only the first match.

Example: semkit read --text "купить диван" replace-text pairs.csv write -
-> купить софа
Example: semkit read --text "Диван" replace-text pairs.csv --by phrase write -
-> Софа

pairs: a file of two columns, what to find and its replacement; the first row is the header, the file is read like `read` does.

The step rewrites the working column; with --as NAME it writes the result to a new column NAME.

options.name: --pairs
options.description: a file of two columns, what to find and its replacement; the first row is the header, the file is read like `read` does.

options.name: --by
--as
options.description: Write the result to a new column NAME and keep the working column as it is.

arguments.name: PAIRS
arguments.description: a file of two columns, what to find and its replacement; the first row is the header, the file is read like `read` does. The same as --pairs PAIRS.
